state:
Data race on HttpBaseChannel::mLoadFlags - written on cache I/O thread

OnCacheEntryCheck runs on the cache IO thread (CHECK_MULTITHREADED flag) and does mLoadFlags |= INHIBIT_CACHING, while the main thread may read mLoadFlags concurrently via GetLoadFlags().

The fix makes mLoadFlags Atomic<uint32_t, Relaxed> in HttpBaseChannel, matching the pattern already used for mStatus, mCanceled, TransferSize
etc. in the same class. Also updates SetCacheFlags() to accept the Atomic reference.

The write only triggers when a no-store cached response is loaded as read-only (offline back-navigation). The main thread is idle in the event loop during this window. On x86/ARM64 the aligned 32-bit RMW is HW-atomic. No security implications.

Data race on HttpBaseChannel::mLoadFlags - written on cache I/O thread

OnCacheEntryCheck runs on the cache IO thread (CHECK_MULTITHREADED flag) and does mLoadFlags |= INHIBIT_CACHING, while the main thread may read mLoadFlags concurrently via GetLoadFlags().

The fix makes mLoadFlags Atomic<uint32_t, Relaxed> in HttpBaseChannel, matching the pattern already used for mStatus, mCanceled, TransferSize
etc. in the same class. Also updates SetCacheFlags() to accept the Atomic reference.

The write only triggers when a no-store cached response is loaded as read-only (offline back-navigation). The main thread is idle in the event loop during this window. On x86/ARM64 the aligned 32-bit RMW is HW-atomic. No security implications.

Routing determination: storage. Regression assessment: not a regression.

state:
Use-after-free in [@ nsDownloader::ConsumeData] when pipe callback synchronously drops last ref during ReadSegments

### Summary

Use-after-free in `nsDownloader::ConsumeData` (`/firefox/netwerk/base/nsDownloader.cpp:87`). `nsDownloader::OnDataAvailable` (line 97) passes raw `this` as the `void*` closure to `ReadSegments` with no kungFuDeathGrip. When the input stream is an `nsPipeInputStream`, draining each segment can synchronously fire an `nsIOutputStreamCallback` (documented behavior when `asyncWait` is called with a null event target — `/firefox/xpcom/io/nsIAsyncOutputStream.idl:71-73`). That synchronous callback can drop the last strong reference to the `nsDownloader`, and the next `ReadSegments` iteration dereferences the dangling closure.

### Affected Code

**File:** `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsDownloader.cpp`, lines 82–98

**Why it's vulnerable:** `ReadSegments` is not an atomic operation. `nsPipeInputStream::ReadSegments` (`/firefox/xpcom/io/nsPipe3.cpp:1388-1447`) iterates once per segment:

`~AutoReadSegment` (`/firefox/xpcom/io/nsPipe3.cpp:516-526`) → `nsPipe::AdvanceReadCursor` (`:700-730`) → `~nsPipeEvents` (`:1206-1211`) → `CallbackHolder::Notify` (`:158-168`):

The synchronous re-entry runs JS that calls `nsStreamListenerTee::Init` (`/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStreamListenerTee.cpp:168`), which assigns `mListener = listener;` — overwriting the last `nsCOMPtr` holding the downloader alive. `nsDownloader::Release` hits refcount 0 and frees the object. The `while (aCount)` loop continues and line 1429 invokes `ConsumeData` with the now-dangling closure.

### Correct Pattern

### Exploit Chain

1. Chrome JS creates an `nsIPipe` with 4 × 512-byte segments and fills it to capacity (2048 bytes).
2. Creates an `nsDownloader` and wraps it in an `nsStreamListenerTee` so that `slTee.mListener` is the only strong reference to the downloader (JS references are nulled and GC/CC forced).
3. Registers `pipeOut.asyncWait(callback, 0, 0, null)`.

3. Registers `pipeOut.asyncWait(callback, 0, 0, null)`.

random immediate connection failures

Steps to reproduce:

Try to open a URL, at least a URL that has been opened recently (e.g. from a few minutes earlier to less than 24 hours earlier).

Actual results:

I sometimes get an immediate "Unable to connect" error. Reloading always works.

Expected results:

I shouldn't get an error.

Note: I've got this issue since at least Firefox 88 in July 2021. Firefox 92 and 94 are also affected. This issue occurs with various websites (e.g. my own website [link] but also lists.gnu.org and some Google search URL), and I could reproduce it with different local networks (SFR FTTH and Free via a mobile hotspot). But note that I'm not even sure that Firefox really attempts to connect. Each time, the failure is immediate, and a reload opens the page instantly.

I had reported the bug in the Debian BTS in July:
[link]

Heap-use-after-free in [@ mozilla::net::BackgroundDataBridgeParent::AddRef] via racing SocketProcessBridgeParent::RecvInitBackgroundDataBridge

SocketProcessBridgeParent::RecvInitBackgroundDataBridge dispatches a lambda to a freshly created background task queue for each incoming message. state:
Data race on TRRService::mParentalControlEnabled

mParentalControlEnabled is a plain bool written on the main thread (Init, nsDNSService::ReloadParentalControlEnabled) and read from DNS resolver threads in nsHostResolver::ComputeEffectiveTRRMode(). The resolver threads hold mQueue.mLock but that doesn't protect TRRService members.

The fix changes mParentalControlEnabled to Atomic<bool, Relaxed>.

Severity: S4 (low). A torn read could cause one DNS resolution to incorrectly use or skip TRR when parental controls status just changed. The next lookup reads the correct value. Parental controls are toggled by the OS or parental control software, not by web content. The bool is HW-atomic on x86/ARM64 anyway.

mParentalControlEnabled is a plain bool written on the main thread (Init, nsDNSService::ReloadParentalControlEnabled) and read from DNS resolver threads in nsHostResolver::ComputeEffectiveTRRMode(). The resolver threads hold mQueue.mLock but that doesn't protect TRRService members.

The fix changes mParentalControlEnabled to Atomic<bool, Relaxed>.

Severity: S4 (low). A torn read could cause one DNS resolution to incorrectly use or skip TRR when parental controls status just changed. The next lookup reads the correct value. Parental controls are toggled by the OS or parental control software, not by web content. The bool is HW-atomic on x86/ARM64 anyway.

Routing determination: network. Regression assessment: not a regression.

state: Heap-Buffer-Overflow through nsStandardURL deserialization from nsIObjectInputStream test.html ### Summary **Out-of-bounds heap read** in `nsStandardURL::ReadPrivate()` at `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.cpp:3425`. The function calls `CheckIfHostIsAscii()` **before** calling `IsValid()` (line 3430), which is the only place where the attacker-controlled `mHost.mPos` offset is bounds-checked against `mSpec.Length()`. `CheckIfHostIsAscii()` → `Host()` performs `mSpec.CharAt(mHost.mPos)` where `CharAt` has only a debug-mode `MOZ_ASSERT` — no release-mode bounds check. A compromised content process can reach this code in the **parent process** by sending a crafted `nsIReferrerInfo` IPC parameter, triggering an arbitrary-offset heap read. ### Affected Code **File:** `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.cpp`, lines 3425–3432 **File:** `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.h`, lines 594–605 **File:** `/firefox/xpcom/string/nsTString.h`, lines 188–191 **Why this is vulnerable:** - `ReadSegment()` (`/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.cpp:1037-1063`) reads `mPos` as a raw `uint32_t` from the stream with **no validation whatsoever**. It only clamps `mLen` if it exceeds `INT32_MAX`. - `IsValid()` at line 248 correctly validates `aSeg.mPos + aSeg.mLen > mSpec.Length()` — but `ReadPrivate` invokes it one step too late. - `MOZ_ASSERT` expands to `do { } while (false)` in non-DEBUG builds (`/firefox/mfbt/Assertions.h:540-542`). - `Substring()` at line 604 actually clamps `startPos` (`/firefox/xpcom/string/nsTDependentSubstring.cpp:19-21`), but the two `CharAt()` calls on line 599 execute **first** with raw unchecked offsets. ### Correct Pattern ### Exploit Chain 1. Compromised content process initiates any network request (`fetch()`, ``, navigation) — all serialize an `nsIReferrerInfo` over IPC. 2. Content process's `ParamTraits::Write` is invoked (the patch hooks here to simulate a compromised renderer).

The function calls `CheckIfHostIsAscii()` **before** calling `IsValid()` (line 3430), which is the only place where the attacker-controlled `mHost.mPos` offset is bounds-checked against `mSpec.Length()`. `CheckIfHostIsAscii()` → `Host()` performs `mSpec.CharAt(mHost.mPos)` where `CharAt` has only a debug-mode `MOZ_ASSERT` — no release-mode bounds check. A compromised content process can reach this code in the **parent process** by sending a crafted `nsIReferrerInfo` IPC parameter, triggering an arbitrary-offset heap read. ### Affected Code **File:** `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.cpp`, lines 3425–3432 **File:** `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.h`, lines 594–605 **File:** `/firefox/xpcom/string/nsTString.h`, lines 188–191 **Why this is vulnerable:** - `ReadSegment()` (`/firefox/netwerk/base/nsStandardURL.cpp:1037-1063`) reads `mPos` as a raw `uint32_t` from the stream with **no validation whatsoever**. It only clamps `mLen` if it exceeds `INT32_MAX`. - `IsValid()` at line 248 correctly validates `aSeg.mPos + aSeg.mLen > mSpec.Length()` — but `ReadPrivate` invokes it one step too late. - `MOZ_ASSERT` expands to `do { } while (false)` in non-DEBUG builds (`/firefox/mfbt/Assertions.h:540-542`). - `Substring()` at line 604 actually clamps `startPos` (`/firefox/xpcom/string/nsTDependentSubstring.cpp:19-21`), but the two `CharAt()` calls on line 599 execute **first** with raw unchecked offsets. ### Correct Pattern ### Exploit Chain 1. Compromised content process initiates any network request (`fetch()`, ``, navigation) — all serialize an `nsIReferrerInfo` over IPC. 2. Content process's `ParamTraits::Write` is invoked (the patch hooks here to simulate a compromised renderer). Routing determination: network. Regression assessment: not a regression.

Firefox removes at sign (@) from UDP links for VLC video player

Steps to reproduce:

Our web-app system generates URLs for UDP multicast video streams that are opened in VLC video player. The URL looks like this: udp://@239.2.3.10:1234 These URLs contain at sign (@) that is being removed by the browser (from Firefox 133) although in the HTML code it is present. This happened recently, it worked on older versions of Firefox.

The meaning of IP address behind @ means the UDP multicast group that should be registered by VLC to receive UDP multicast packets. Before the @ sign there is usually nothing which means that VLC should listen on all local interfaces.

Example of URL with @: [link] Hover the mouse over the generated URL and see that the @ was removed.

Description of multicast UDP URLs: [link]

The problem is also reported and described here: [link]

Actual results:

The VLC is opened, but the @ is not passed to it so the video does not play.

Expected results:

It should work like in older Firefox releases: open VLC with full URL including the @ and play video. It worked on version 132.

state:
URL parsing changes allowing OriginAttributes spoofing

In bug 1873973, we changed the parsing in `nsStandardURL` such that the `^` character is no longer escaped within paths. This unfortunately opens a security hole in our OriginAttributes infrastructure, which could potentially allow someone to spoof origin attributes.

In bug 1172080, we changed the separating character in origin strings from the `!` character to the `^` character because the `!` character was not guaranteed to be escaped by `nsStandardURL`, leading to a potential valid URL appearing to have originattributes present. Now that we do not escape `^` in file paths this same bug can occur again but with the `^` character, allowing evil paths like (e.g. `file:///tmp/foo^userContextId=1`).

See also the comment [link] which has extra comments about the escaping requirements on Networking URLs.

This situation is potentially even worse for Thunderbird, as they support `ORIGIN_IS_FULL_SPEC`, which means that more URI types include the full path within their `originNoSuffix` definition.

Unfortunately, changing the separating character (as we did last time) or making it mandatory for all origin serializations will be quite difficult, as these origin strings are serialized into the profile in a large number of places.

In bug 1172080, we changed the separating character in origin strings from the `!` character to the `^` character because the `!` character was not guaranteed to be escaped by `nsStandardURL`, leading to a potential valid URL appearing to have originattributes present. Now that we do not escape `^` in file paths this same bug can occur again but with the `^` character, allowing evil paths like (e.g. `file:///tmp/foo^userContextId=1`).

See also the comment [link] which has extra comments about the escaping requirements on Networking URLs.

This situation is potentially even worse for Thunderbird, as they support `ORIGIN_IS_FULL_SPEC`, which means that more URI types include the full path within their `originNoSuffix` definition.

Unfortunately, changing the separating character (as we did last time) or making it mandatory for all origin serializations will be quite difficult, as these origin strings are serialized into the profile in a large number of places.

Routing determination: network. Regression assessment: regression.

state:
Predictable redirect registrar IDs allow cross-process redirected channel attachment

fix.patch

## Description
RedirectChannelRegistrar and BackgroundChannelRegistrar accept child-supplied channel IDs without binding them to the intended ContentParent. The redirect registrar ID is predictable and truncated through uint32_t IPC/IDL surfaces, allowing a compromised content process to race a forged redirected channel attachment for another process's redirect. A successful race can deliver the victim redirect's parent network response events to the attacker's content process; otherwise it can abort or stall the victim redirect.

## Discovery / Environment
Found by source audit of the redirect IPC path using searchfox-cli and local code review. I traced nsContentUtils::GenerateLoadIdentifier() to DocumentLoadListener::RedirectToRealChannel and HttpChannelParent::StartRedirect, then followed the child-controlled registrarId through PHttpChannel::Redirect1Begin, nsIChildChannel::ConnectParent, PNecko::ConnectBaseChannel, RedirectChannelRegistrar::LinkChannels, and BackgroundChannelRegistrar::LinkBackgroundChannel.

The patch was build-checked locally with ./mach build export and ./mach build binaries.

state:
SameSite cookies are set by cross-site iframe navigations

poc.js

Hello,

As part of a research project at TU Wien, we are assessing the security implications of WPT tests. We encountered an inconsistency in Firefox, which allows setting SameSite=Strict and Lax cookies from cross-site navigations. This inconsistency allows a gadget attacker (e.g., an ad embedded as an iframe in a benign website, `good.com`) to deauthenticate users. When paired with a same-site attacker scenario (e.g., when the attacker controls a subdomain of the target website such as `atk.good.com`), this inconsistency enables stealthy cookie-tossing attacks, which an attacker could leverage to perform more effective session fixation or CSRF token fixation attacks by removing the need for the victim to navigate to the attacker-controlled subdomain.

The deauth attack has the following flow:
1. User navigates to `good.com`
2. `good.com` sets a cookie `auth=1; SameSite=Strict` and embeds `evil.com`.
3. `evil.com` navigates itself to `good.com/logout`, e.g., via `window.location.href="[link] which overwrites the `auth` cookie with `auth=0; SameSite=Strict`.

The `auth` cookie (SameSite=Strict or Lax) is set for `good.com` from a non-top-level cross-origin navigation originating from `evil.com`. In contrast with Firefox, Chrome does not set these cookies. Although not explicitly mentioned by [rfc6265bis]([link] we would argue that Chrome's behavior is more in line with the semantics and expectations of SameSite cookies.

The complete NodeJS code of the PoC is attached to this vulnerability report.

This behavior is captured by the (failing) WPT test: [setcookie-navigation.https.html]([link] in particular, the subtest "Cross-site to same-site iframe navigation should only be able to set SameSite=None cookies".

We searched Bugzilla for related issues but found only two bug reports (bug#1692207 and bug#1572607) referencing this test without a clear discussion of its security implications.

Concurrent DNS lookups for different hosts in a child process can cancel or complete the wrong request

`ChildDNSService::GetDNSRecordHashKey` (`netwerk/dns/ChildDNSService.cpp`) calls `aHashKey.Assign(aHost)` and then `aHashKey.Assign(aTrrServer)`, so the host name is overwritten and never becomes part of the key.

When the same listener resolves two different hosts at the same time with the same flags, type, origin attributes and TRR server, both requests get the same `mPendingRequests` key. `CancelAsyncResolve` and `NotifyRequestDone` can then act on the wrong request.

Fix: the second call should be `Append`.

Content-Disposition filename truncation leads to Reflected File Download

User-Agent:

When handling filename directive in the Content-Disposition header, the filename would be truncated if the token contains a NULL character and only the first part is kept: `filename.exe<NULL>.txt` -> `filename.exe`
This behavior makes Firefox users vulnerable to reflected file download (RFD). For instance, CVE-2022-36359[1] in Django that has been patched[2] is still exploitable on Firefox because the filename truncation provides a trivial way to manipulate and bypass extension checking/appending on the server side. These RFD vulnerabilities such as CVE-2022-36359, CVE-2015-5211[3] and CVE-2020-5398[4] in Spring Frameworks are all rated as High or Important in severity by the project maintainers.
More about RFD: [link]

I know the vulnerability exists partly because Django allows invalid characters (RFC 2616 I suppose) in the filename. That said, this can only be addressed reliably from the client side. I believe it would be reasonable to stop accepting responses with invalid headers.

Given `request.GET.get('filename') = file.cmd%00`, Firefox would download the file `file.cmd` instead of `file.cmd.pdf` while Chromium and Safari threw an error (ERR_INVALID_HTTP_RESPONSE) and refused to open the page in this case.

[3] [link]
[4] [link]

User-Agent:

When handling filename directive in the Content-Disposition header, the filename would be truncated if the token contains a NULL character and only the first part is kept: `filename.exe<NULL>.txt` -> `filename.exe`
This behavior makes Firefox users vulnerable to reflected file download (RFD). For instance, CVE-2022-36359[1] in Django that has been patched[2] is still exploitable on Firefox because the filename truncation provides a trivial way to manipulate and bypass extension checking/appending on the server side. These RFD vulnerabilities such as CVE-2022-36359, CVE-2015-5211[3] and CVE-2020-5398[4] in Spring Frameworks are all rated as High or Important in severity by the project maintainers.
More about RFD: [link]

I know the vulnerability exists partly because Django allows invalid characters (RFC 2616 I suppose) in the filename. That said, this can only be addressed reliably from the client side. I believe it would be reasonable to stop accepting responses with invalid headers.

Given `request.GET.get('filename') = file.cmd%00`, Firefox would download the file `file.cmd` instead of `file.cmd.pdf` while Chromium and Safari threw an error (ERR_INVALID_HTTP_RESPONSE) and refused to open the page in this case.

state:
When following cross-origin redirect, Firefox sends preflight request with "Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization" even though "Authorization" header will never be forwarded.

preflight-request.png

Steps to reproduce:

Given a client and a server (A) on the same origin and a server (B) on a different origin.

- The client sends GET request with "Authorization" header to the server (A).
- The server (A) responds with status code 3xx and "Location" header (i.e. redirect to a resource on the server (B)).

Note that on cross-origin redirect, Firefox remove "Authorization" header:
[link]

Actual results:

- Firefox sends preflight (i.e method=OPTIONS) request to the server (B) with "Access-Control-Request-Headers" header set to "authorization".
- Firefox sends the actual request (i.e. method=GET) to the server (B) without "Authorization" header.

Expected results:

- Firefox sends preflight (i.e method=OPTIONS) request to the server (B) without "Access-Control-Request-Headers" header set to "authorization", because the "Authorization" header will never be forwarded (base case: if simple, the request is not send at all).
- Firefox sends the actual request (i.e. method=GET) to the server (B) without "Authorization" header.

state:
Transactions could be dropped when HappyEyeballsConnectionAttempt::Abandon is called

When two concurrent requests each enter a Happy Eyeballs 0-RTT race, `ZeroRttHandle::Do0RTT` removes both real transactions from the connection manager’s pending queue via `LockInRealTxnFromPendingQueue`. If one race wins and calls `MakeAllDontReuseExcept() → CloseAllConnectionAttempts()`, the other HappyEyeballsConnectionAttempt’s Abandon() is triggered. At that point, the transaction is neither in the pending queue nor attached to any connection, and Abandon() neither closes nor re-queues it. As a result, the channel waits indefinitely and eventually times out with NS_BINDING_ABORTED.

There appear to be a number of issues with locking for nsInputStreamPump. I have some changes that quiet all the thread-safety warnings, however...

state:
Partitioned cookies no longer sent to other localhost domains

Steps to reproduce:

Set a partitioned cookie (that is, a cookie with the Partitioned attribute) on one localhost origin (e.g. [link]

Open a page on a different localhost origin (e.g. [link]

Actual results:

The page in the second localhost origin is not sent the cookie from the first origin. Also, the cookie cannot be seen in the Storage -> Cookies tab for either origin.

Expected results:

The cookie from the first origin should have been sent with the request to the second, and the cookie should be visible in the Storage -> Cookies tab.

Removing the Paritioned attribute, testing with non-localhost origins with the Domain attribute set, or repeating this test in Chrome causes the cookie to be sent to the second origin as expected. (Though the cookie still cannot be seen in the second case, where it is Partitioned on a non-localhost site).

[link]

but not mTotalBytesWritten.

state:
ObliviousHttpService recursive GetService during startup

nsDNSService::Init gets the OHTTP service partway through its own setup, before mTrrService exists. The ObliviousHttpService constructor called ReadPrefs("*"), which went straight into FetchConfig and opened an HTTP channel. That channel's DNS prefetch called back into the DNS service hile it was still being created:
- canUseHTTPSRRonNetwork asked for the DNS service again, which caused the "Recursive GetService!" assertion.
- Going through nsDNSPrefetch, NativeLookup called TRRService::Get()->IsExcludedFromTRR while TRRService was still null.

Dispatching FetchConfig instead of directly calling AsyncOpen would avoid the cycle.

ODoH memory leak when internet connection lost in TRR-only mode, infinite loop trying to update ODoHConfigs.

odoh-leak-no-internet-log.txt

STR:
1. Enable ODoH in TRR-only mode (`network.trr.mode = 3`).
2. Disconnect internet.

├────101.78 MB (04.09%) ++ (31 tiny)
├─────69.11 MB (02.78%) -- heap-overhead
│ ├──61.04 MB (02.45%) ── bookkeeping
│ └───8.07 MB (00.32%) ++ (3 tiny)
└─────31.71 MB (01.28%) ++ js-non-window

state:
Firefox 154's first launch after updating from 153 left the QuotaManager (storage.sqlite) database corrupt

Steps to reproduce:

On starting up FIrefox this morning many sites were not working, e.g. no profile info on X, only a bare prompt box on Gemini that didn't accept intput, bloomberg.com reporting load failures, etc. On investigation I saw his was under the 153 -> 154 update last night. Clearing site data, disabling extensions did not help - only starting in Troubleshoot mode

Doing localStorage.setItem('t','1') on the console failed with NS_ERROR_FAILURE

Actual results:

I investigated with Claude and it turns out this was corruption in storage.sqlite. Removing that to allow a rebuild resolved the issue. Opus 4.8's summary of what happened and root cause is below. I submit this because it might be helpful to someone who comes across this same issue.

Summary: After updating 153.0 -> 154.0, QuotaManager's storage.sqlite became corrupt (inconsistent
freelist), so QuotaManager fails to initialize and ALL Web Storage / IndexedDB / Cache API calls throw
NS_ERROR_FAILURE on every site. No filesystem corruption, no SQLite corruption anywhere else, no crash,
no profile sync. Moving storage.sqlite out (QM rebuilds it) fixes it — CONFIRMED.

Component: Core :: Storage: Quota Manager
Firefox: 154.0, Mozilla official tarball build (not Snap/deb)
OS: Ubuntu 24.04, X11, XFCE, ext4
Onset: immediately after the 153 -> 154 update (late evening); worked fine on 153 earlier that day.
Related: bug 1996210 (same QM-init-failure symptom, attributed to filesystem corruption — NOT the case
here), bug 1862215 (broad NS_ERROR_FAILURE localStorage report), bug 1881526 (no reporting for broken
origins on disk).

[Symptom] SPA sites render ~1s then fall back to their client-side error page. Console shows localStorage
read/write throwing NS_ERROR_FAILURE (first- and third-party), and React error #423 (hydration dies).
`localStorage.setItem('t','1')` throws NS_ERROR_FAILURE.

state:
Firefox 154's first launch after updating from 153 left the QuotaManager (storage.sqlite) database corrupt

Steps to reproduce:

On starting up FIrefox this morning many sites were not working, e.g. no profile info on X, only a bare prompt box on Gemini that didn't accept intput, bloomberg.com reporting load failures, etc. On investigation I saw his was under the 153 -> 154 update last night. Clearing site data, disabling extensions did not help - only starting in Troubleshoot mode

Doing localStorage.setItem('t','1') on the console failed with NS_ERROR_FAILURE

Actual results:

I investigated with Claude and it turns out this was corruption in storage.sqlite. Removing that to allow a rebuild resolved the issue. Opus 4.8's summary of what happened and root cause is below. I submit this because it might be helpful to someone who comes across this same issue.

Summary: After updating 153.0 -> 154.0, QuotaManager's storage.sqlite became corrupt (inconsistent
freelist), so QuotaManager fails to initialize and ALL Web Storage / IndexedDB / Cache API calls throw
NS_ERROR_FAILURE on every site. No filesystem corruption, no SQLite corruption anywhere else, no crash,
no profile sync. Moving storage.sqlite out (QM rebuilds it) fixes it — CONFIRMED.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Firefox 84.0.2 on macOS 11.1, running in ARM mode

2. Configured parameters for Kerberos SPENGO:

network.negotiate-auth.trusted-uris: https://

3. Open a webpage with SPNEGO authentication. I'm using Keycloak as the authentication server, federated with AD domain, with SPNEGO enabled.

Additional observations:

Under Rosetta, it works correctly. The crash only happens in ARM mode.

Actual results:

Expected results:

state:
FireFox does not expect late Data/Push on h2 connection and flare up with RST(1) in response

Steps to reproduce:

[link]

1. deploy app and access over http2
2. spam refresh
3. either wait for "zero byte" or capture traffic with wireshark( need to capture ssl keys - [link] )

Actual results:

At some point, WFLY/UNDERTOW trigger rapid RST defense and break connection.
This happens because on HttpPush attempts, for cached resources FF sends RST(7) frame, but does not expect late push frames that can already be scheduled and on the way. Those frames trigger flare of RST(1). This happens on local machine, with network bigger TTL, it can be more pronounced, essentially turning FF into ~Rapid RST attacker.

Expected results:

FF should keep track of streams it reset and have configurable:
- at least grace period during which late DATA/Push wont be considered a protocol error
- possibly a way or limit of how many RST(1) can be sent in period of time(maybe configurable?)

REF: [link]
"However, after sending the RST_STREAM, the sending endpoint MUST be prepared to receive and process additional frames sent on the stream that might have been sent by the peer prior to the arrival of the RST_STREAM."

state:
Heap use-after-free in [@ mozilla::net::TokenBucketCancelable::Fire] in the socket process via unvalidated nsresult in PHttpConnectionMgr::CancelTransaction

PHttpConnectionMgr::CancelTransaction(PHttpTransaction aTrans, nsresult aReason) carries a cancellation status that originates, unvalidated, from the content process: HttpChannelParent::RecvCancel accepts an arbitrary content-supplied nsresult and nsHttpChannel/HttpConnectionMgrParent relay it verbatim to the socket process. A compromised content process can therefore inject the internal sentinel failure code NS_BINDING_RETARGETED (0x804B0004), which content must never control: in the socket process, nsHttpTransaction::Close(NS_BINDING_RETARGETED) deliberately returns early (this sentinel is reserved for the WebSocket upgrade machinery to detach a transaction without closing it) and skips the mTokenBucketCancel->Cancel() cleanup.

The request-pacing token bucket (EventTokenBucket, enabled by default: network.http.pacing.requests.enabled=true, hz=80, burst=10) holds a TokenBucketCancelable whose mEvent member is a RAW ATokenBucketEvent* pointer to the nsHttpTransaction. The lifetime contract is that the transaction always cancels this entry from nsHttpTransaction::Close() before it can be destroyed. The injected sentinel breaks that contract: when the canceled channel is torn down, the PHttpTransaction actor's destruction (HttpTransactionChild::ActorDestroy, on the socket-process main thread) drops the last reference and ~nsHttpTransaction runs off the socket thread, where — in release builds, guarded only by a MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT that is compiled out — the cancelable is silently dropped without being canceled. The freed transaction's address remains queued in the token bucket; when the pacing timer next fires, TokenBucketCancelable::Fire() performs the virtual call mEvent->OnTokenBucketAdmitted() on the freed nsHttpTransaction.

The request-pacing token bucket (EventTokenBucket, enabled by default: network.http.pacing.requests.enabled=true, hz=80, burst=10) holds a TokenBucketCancelable whose mEvent member is a RAW ATokenBucketEvent* pointer to the nsHttpTransaction. The lifetime contract is that the transaction always cancels this entry from nsHttpTransaction::Close() before it can be destroyed. The injected sentinel breaks that contract: when the canceled channel is torn down, the PHttpTransaction actor's destruction (HttpTransactionChild::ActorDestroy, on the socket-process main thread) drops the last reference and ~nsHttpTransaction runs off the socket thread, where — in release builds, guarded only by a MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT that is compiled out — the cancelable is silently dropped without being canceled. The freed transaction's address remains queued in the token bucket; when the pacing timer next fires, TokenBucketCancelable::Fire() performs the virtual call mEvent->OnTokenBucketAdmitted() on the freed nsHttpTransaction.

nsHostRecord::mTRRSuccess and nsHostRecord::mNativeSuccess are not reset before a new lookup

Looking at how [nsHostRecord::mTRRSuccess]([link] is used in our code, it's used as a `bool`, but it's actually a `uint8_t` and is increased [here]([link]

Sending multiple (unknown) cookies with same name

collection of screenshots

Steps to reproduce:

Background: I am using Firefox 131 (64bit) on Windows 10 towards my own local web server.

I am visiting a page / refreshing a page.

Actual results:

On the initial HTTP GET request to fetch the page/resource, Firefox is sending the cookie header:

Cookie: keystone-session-1=zxy9ifgh; keystone-session-1=o1ukqfle

Meaning two cookies with the same name.

However, when looking at my saved Cookies in the Storage tab in Developer Tools, can only see one single cookie.

At any given time there is only one Cookie present in Developer Tools.

Expected results:

Firefox should only send one cookie, the one that is present in the Storage Cookies tab.

I don't understand / I cannot see where the cookie "keystone-session-1=zxy9ifgh;" is coming from, but it is added to all requests.

state:
Windows Firefox Kerberos authentication broken with Extended protection set to allow on ADFS server with a SHA384 SSL certificate

Steps to reproduce:

1. Upgrade ADFS Communication and SSL certificate to SHA384
2. Verify that ExtendedProtectionCheck is set to Allow on the ADFS service. Get-AdfsProperties| select ExtendedProtectionTokenCheck
3. From a Domain Joined Windows client attempt to access a SAML configured website using Windows Firefox from internal network.

Actual results:

User is greeted with a prompt for username and password.
Manually entering the username and password fails and leads to the same prompt from the ADFS server.

Similar to [link] but specific only when using SHA384 certificate.

Expected results:

The user should have been directed to the ADFS server and complete the authentication using Windows Integrated Authentication.
User should have then been redirected to the website with the appropriate authentication and access

state:
Client code for "Firefox/100.0" UA string experiment does not work across restarts

The Nimbus client code added in bug 1719070 does not work across browser restarts, it just falls back to the default User Agent string. From my naive and uninformed understanding of [the implementation in `nsHttpHandler.cpp`]([link] it seems like this is caused by the UA experiment only being applied whenever `NimbusFeatures::OnUpdate` fires, which is not the case for browser restarts. This assumption would be consistent with the observation that changing the `nimbus.syncdatastore.firefox100.firefoxVersion` pref to any other value during runtime immediately makes the change go into effect (until the next restart).

**STR:**

2. in the DevTools console on that site run

**Actual result:** 151

Being off by one isn't that big a deal because the quota is more of a suggestion in the spec. But we differ from Chrome and that might have unwanted effects on some site someday.

state:
Don't use a special longer idle timeout for the DoH HTTP/3 connection

Bug 1949422 gave the DoH HTTP/3 connection its own idle timeout, the pref network.trr.idle_timeout_for_http3_conn, set to 400s on early beta and earlier (30s otherwise) to improve connection reuse. Every other HTTP/3 connection uses network.http.http3.idle_timeout (30s).

400s is close to seven minutes, and a window that long causes two problems.

NAT rebinding: neqo only sends keep-alive pings while a request stream is open, so an idle DoH connection sends nothing. RFC 4787 asks for a NAT UDP mapping lifetime of at least two minutes and recommends five, but many home routers use less, and RFC 8085 notes that a significant fraction of deployed middleboxes use shorter timeouts still. Once the connection sits idle past the router's UDP timeout the mapping is dropped and return traffic is lost; with a 400s idle timeout the connection can stay dead for minutes before it is torn down and rebuilt.

Black holes: even with a request in flight, keep-alive does not shorten the teardown. See Bug 2060483 for details.

Proposal: drop the special case so the DoH connection uses the same 30s idle timeout as other HTTP/3 connections. 30s sits below common NAT UDP timeouts and keeps a dead connection from lingering. The general idle-timeout plumbing that bug 1949422 added is kept, only the DoH-specific value is removed.

We can re-introduce the long timeout with Bug 2060483.

RFC 4787 REQ-5: [link]
RFC 8085 section 3.5: [link]

Platform: Desktop
Version: Firefox Nightly 153.0a1 (commit `6e5c51c815fd4f0bb04bdc49a5124a6721c5db3a`)

### Summary

When a Private Browsing Mode IndexedDB Blob is sent from the parent process to a content process, Firefox serializes enough encrypted-stream material for the content side to reconstruct the stream. A compromised content process can use those IPC parameters to read the raw encrypted base stream and decrypt the rounded final-block payload, including the hidden bytes after `ActualPayloadLength()`.

Normal Blob / IndexedDB readback returns only the logical Blob contents, so ordinary web content does not see those bytes. The issue is that the IPC-delivered stream material lets a compromised content process recover up to 15 bytes beyond the logical final payload of each affected partial encrypted file block.

### Steps to Reproduce

The attached patch has three proof-only pieces:

1. A content-process probe in `dom/quota/DecryptingInputStream_impl.h` at `DecryptingInputStream::Deserialize()`. The probe runs in the patched content process and uses only the received `EncryptedFileInputStreamParams` key and the deserialized raw base stream to decrypt the final encrypted block.
2. A proof seed in `dom/quota/EncryptingOutputStream_impl.h`. It fills the newly allocated plaintext buffer with `0xa0 + (offset & 0x0f)` before the logical write. A one-byte Blob overwrites only `mBuffer[0]`, so `mBuffer[1..15]` remains as known pre-encryption buffer content.
3. A browser-chrome test `dom/indexedDB/test/browser_encrypted_tail_probe.js` that opens a private window, stores a one-byte Blob in IndexedDB, then reads the Blob back to force the parent-to-child `RemoteLazyInputStream` path.

The one-byte Blob creates a partial final encrypted block for the real IndexedDB encrypted stream block size:

state:
Images intermittently don't load in some cases

Broken Request

As discussed, I am encountering sporadic situations where certain images don't load (so far on Amazon and Ebay).

The bug was always intermittent and the request in network console does not show a return code and transferred/size are both "0 B". However, on Ebay it consistently reproduced for a while until it went away. The last time I was able to reproduce it, I had my user agent switched using "Mobile View Switcher" and was visiting with that turned on. Turning it off made the images work immediately, turning it back on they still worked (caches were off).

I was able to capture a network log, will send via email to :kershaw.

### Summary

Heap use-after-free via cross-thread data race in `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsDNSPrefetch.cpp` line 157. `nsDNSPrefetch::OnLookupComplete` (main thread) calls `do_QueryReferent(mListener)` on a non-threadsafe `nsWeakReference` whose referent (`nsHttpChannel`) can be destroyed concurrently on a background thread. `nsWeakReference::QueryReferent` reads `mObject` without synchronization; if the read occurs while `~nsHttpChannel` is running (before the `~nsSupportsWeakReference` base destructor clears `mObject`), it returns a pointer to a mid-destruction object. `QueryInterface`/`AddRef` succeed on the dying object, but the already-committed destructor chain proceeds to `operator delete`, leaving a dangling `nsIDNSListener*` that `listener->OnLookupComplete(...)` calls through.

### Affected Code

**File:** `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsDNSPrefetch.cpp`, lines 151–163

**Why this is vulnerable:**

`mListener` is an `nsWeakPtr` (declared in `/firefox/netwerk/base/nsDNSPrefetch.h:66`) holding an `nsWeakReference` proxy for an `nsHttpChannel`. The `nsWeakReference` class at `/firefox/xpcom/base/nsWeakReference.cpp:13-44` uses `NS_DECL_ISUPPORTS` (line 16) — non-threadsafe refcounting — and stores the referent pointer in a plain `nsISupports* mObject` field (`/firefox/xpcom/base/nsIWeakReference.idl:87`).

`nsIWeakReference::QueryReferent` at `/firefox/xpcom/base/nsWeakReference.cpp:129-138`:

Meanwhile, `~nsSupportsWeakReference` at `/firefox/xpcom/base/nsWeakReference.h:41-43` calls `ClearWeakReferences()` → `mProxy->NoticeReferentDestruction()` → `mObject = nullptr` (`/firefox/xpcom/base/nsWeakReference.cpp:42`) — a plain non-atomic store from whatever thread is running the destructor.

**Why the destructor can run off-main-thread:**

state:
Expose X-Firefox-Http3 header in release builds

Steps to reproduce:

Extension authors would like to be able to determine whether a page was loaded over HTTP/3. Extensions can do this for HTTP/2 by checking for the presence of the synthetic X-Firefox-Spdy header which Firefox adds to responses when the page is loaded over HTTP/2.

Currently the Network Inspector shows a column indicating whether a page was loaded over HTTP/3, but this is not exposed in a way that extensions can access. A patch[1] was landed that exposes this value via a new synthetic header, "X-Firefox-Http3", however the code that adds that header is only present in debug builds.

[1]: [link]

Actual results:

Currently extensions have no way to programmatically determine if a page was loaded over HTTP/3. Extensions can determine when website advertises HTTP/3 support via the Alt-Svc header but its presence can not be a guarantee that request did load via HTTP/3.

Expected results:

Extensions should be able to inspect the synthetic X-Firefox-Http3 header in the response to determine if a page was loaded over HTTP/3.

Shift-reload web page that is not responding properly to 0RTT request. Capture timings in Developer Tools and with network capture. Pay attention to wall clock when reload command issued and when the first HTTP request fills in its timing.

Actual results:

Timings in developer tools do not match timings in network capture or on wall clock.

In my case, there was a 10 second timeout for the initial connection, and then Firefox tried again and the request completed. The wall clock said that this took approximately 11 seconds, but the Developer Tools timings said 20.72 seconds. It also claimed that DNS resolution took 10.16 seconds, but no DNS resolution occurred over the network and the initial HTTP request was made well within a second of the reload being issued. (Which, to be clear, would be very difficult if it didn't have an IP to connect to until 10 seconds later.)

Expected results:

The timings in Firefox's Developer Tools should reflect reality.

state:
Firefox VPN leaks DNS HTTPS record queries outside the VPN tunnel for schemeless domains (URL without protocol) typed into the address bar

# Description

The Firefox browser comes with a built-in VPN as of Firefox 149. [link] The built-in VPN tunnels user web and DNS traffic through Mozilla VPN infrastructure when enabled.

If a user types a domain or URL directly into the address bar without including the https:// protocol prefix, such as [link] or [link] Firefox appears to send an HTTPS DNS query for the typed address which travels outside of the VPN tunnel. The query for the HTTPS record is sent unencrypted and visible in cleartext, permitting a hostile network actor to observe what site the user is attempting to visit through the VPN.

Firefox does not appear to send an HTTPS DNS query if the user explicitly types the "[link] prefix before the address, such as entering [link] This makes sense, as the DNS query is looking for an HTTPS endpoint, but if the user enters an HTTPS URL then Firefox has no need to lookup if the destination has an HTTPS record.

DoH affects this vulnerability as HTTPS queries are sent over DoH by default. However, Firefox only enforces DoH if the user explicitly configures it. Firefox's default configuration falls back to normal unencrypted DNS traffic if connectivity to DoH severs is blocked or if Firefox receives an NXDOMAIN response for the canary domain use-application-dns.net. A hostile network can tamper with the DNS response for the canary domain or block connectivity to DoH servers. Doing either coerces Firefox into falling back to cleartext UDP DNS traffic which can then be seen by the hostile network.

The vulnerability impacts the confidentiality of the user's VPN session. The user's VPN browsing activity is no longer completely private and is disclosed to untrusted networks.

# Reproduction

You will need
- A Windows or Linux system with Firefox browser installed. The browser needs to have the VPN client enabled.

Since this is triggered by a pref change, this is probably a sec-low; at worst a moderate.

Steps to reproduce:

Tried to access YouTube.

Sometimes the website does not load at all (Firefox shows it can't connect to the website). Other times, while I am already at YouTube, some elements stop loading and a disconnection message appears. Restarting the browser solves the problem for a while. Other websites can still be accessed normally (even Google ones) when the problem happens.

Expected results:

The website should be accessible normally without disconnection and without restarting the browser.

The socket thread in the content process calls poll / select for no good reason

Profile: [link]

The socket thread has a special event loop: It puts a runnable called `nsSocketTransportService` as the "initial runnable" on an nsThread, and that runnable runs its own event loop so that it can interleave runnable processing with socket response processing.

This extra handling is fine in the parent process or socket process, but it seems rather unnecessary in the content process. Additionally it probably contributes majorly to the slowdown we see on macOS in `select` (bug 1709175).

Can we just switch to a regular nsThread event loop in content process socket threads?

# Null dereference in `nsHttpChannel::CancelInternal` via async ORB callback

## Summary

A remote server can crash the **Firefox parent process** with a null-pointer
dereference by serving a cross-origin `<script>` response that combines
`Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with a lying `Content-Length` header, triggering
`nsHttpChannel`'s concurrent-cache-write-interrupted recovery path which
`std::move()`s `mResponseHead` to null and falls through without restoring
it — after which the Opaque Response Blocker's async JavaScript-validation
callback fires, sets `mChannelBlockedByOpaqueResponse`, and calls `Cancel()`,
reaching an unguarded `mResponseHead->ClearHeaders()`.

| | |
|---|---|
| **File** | `netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp` |
| **Crash site** | Line 7445 (`mResponseHead->ClearHeaders()`) |
| **Root cause** | Line 10557 (`std::move(mResponseHead)`) + line 10581 fallthrough |
| **Bug class** | Null pointer dereference (parent process) |
| **ASan signature** | `SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000408` |
| **Reachable from** | Web content (cross-origin `<script src>`) |
| **Reproducer** | `brain/tests/nsHttpChannel/test.html` + `server.py` |
| **Default prefs** | All required prefs default-on for Desktop |

## The bug

### Crash site — `nsHttpChannel.cpp:7444-7446`

There is a sibling at `nsHttpChannel.cpp:10696-10698` with the same unguarded
pattern inside `ContinueOnStopRequest`.

### Root cause — `nsHttpChannel.cpp:10543-10586`

`MaybeSetupByteRangeRequest(size, contentLength, true)` fails when
`IsResumable(size, contentLength, true)` is false. `IsResumable` checks
`(partialLen < contentLength)` first — so when `size >= contentLength`, it
immediately returns false and we hit the fallthrough.

The code assumes "interrupted write" means `size < contentLength`.

state:
xircom_tulip_cb.c lock-up with high traffic

Most recent kernel where this bug did not occur: 2.6

Problem Description:

The current implementation of xircom_tulip_cb.c locks up quite reproducable
on my laptop (yenta_socket) almost every time after a few MB of high
throughput. Soon the driver shows the message:

xircom_tulip_cb: outl_CSR6 too many attempts,csr5=0x600f8046

and after a few of them the driver locks up, with the only remedy
being a reload of the driver.
This behavior renders the NIC part of the card unusable for all
but the slowest of transfers.
Turning the CSR6 command register wait function (the card is picky about
the times those registers are accessed) from a constant to a linear
function solves the problems (one-line patch attached). The card is running
smoothly now.

Kernel 2.6 does not suffer from this bug IIRC. I think the complete
driver is different.

Problem Description:

The current implementation of xircom_tulip_cb.c locks up quite reproducable
on my laptop (yenta_socket) almost every time after a few MB of high
throughput. Soon the driver shows the message:

xircom_tulip_cb: outl_CSR6 too many attempts,csr5=0x600f8046

and after a few of them the driver locks up, with the only remedy
being a reload of the driver.
This behavior renders the NIC part of the card unusable for all
but the slowest of transfers.
Turning the CSR6 command register wait function (the card is picky about
the times those registers are accessed) from a constant to a linear
function solves the problems (one-line patch attached). The card is running
smoothly now.

Kernel 2.6 does not suffer from this bug IIRC. I think the complete
driver is different.

state:
With SLUB debugging enabled and 'slub_debug=P' as a boot option, p54usb cannot be unloaded

Latest working kernel version: None
Earliest failing kernel version: All
Distribution: openSUSE 11.0
Hardware Environment: x86_64
Software Environment: p54usb
Problem Description: If SLUB is used with debugging turned on and the 'slub_debug=P' boot option is used, the command 'modprobe -r p54usb' hangs. No dump is produced. On PPC platforms, the system freezes. This is thought to be essentially equivalent to the problem found for rtl8187 in Bugzilla Entry #12185. Certainly, the fix that works for that device fixes p54usb. Both fixes are being submitted through wireless-testing.

Steps to reproduce: Enable SLUB debugging, boot with the option 'slub_debug=P', and 'modprobe -r p54usb'.

state:
iwlwifi fails to start on Intel Wireless-AC 9560

dmesg log

I just got a ThinkPad X1 Carbon 7th Gen, which comes with a Intel® Dual-Band 9560 802.11 AC (according to [link] I installed Arch Linux on it, and I didn't notice a problem until I booted into it for the first time. That is, while I was running off of the USB stick, wifi worked just fine. But each time I boot into my laptop, I see a bunch of logs for iwlwifi written over the login prompt (see the attached file for the full dmesg log). The main errors seem to be:
Collecting data: trigger 15 fired.
Microcode SW error detected. Restarting 0x0
and later:
Failed to start RT ucode: -110
Firmware not running - cannot dump error
Failed to run INIT ucode: -110

This is possibly the same bug as [link] although the comments there indicate a patch has been merged to kernel 5.5, and I still get the error even though I'm on 5.5.8. I've also tried using the linux-lts kernel, with the same results.

Other things that I don't get:
- Like one of the users in that bug's thread, lspci misidentifies my network card as version 9462. (This happens when I boot into the USB drive too, so I don't think that's the problem.)
- The drivers page ([link] indicates that both 9462 and 9560 use the iwldvm module, but the iwlwifi logs say that it loads iwlmvm ("loaded firmware version 48.4fa0041f.0 op_mode iwlmvm"). This is also what lsmod reports.

I'm pretty stumped.

state:
Attempt to mount floppy fails with mount: /dev/fd0 is not a valid block device

Up to and including 2.6.39-rc7, the root user can mount a floppy in a standard PC floppy drive by issuing "mount /dev/fd0 /mnt/floppy". An ordinary user cannot do this (even with a fstab mount entry) due to bug #28522.

Starting with 2.6.39, if root tries to do the same operation, this is the output:

[email] ~]# mount /dev/fd0 /mnt/floppy/
mount: /dev/fd0 is not a valid block device

No I/O is ever attempted on the floppy drive.

To reproduce:

1) Boot 2.6.39 in x86_64 machine with a standard floppy drive (not USB, not parport) and no floppy inserted in the drive.
2) After boot finishes, insert floppy in drive
3) Attempt (as root) to mount the floppy.

Actual results:
mount: /dev/fd0 is not a valid block device
No I/O attempted on drive.

Expected results:
Mount should be successful, or at least I/O should be attempted on the drive.

Any attempt to access /dev/fd0 (such as dd) is affected in the same way.

A strace on mount shows that the open() operation on /dev/fd0 fails with ENXIO, as well as the actual mount() operation.

Bisection on this bug points to the following commit:
commit 9fd097b14918875bd6f125ed699d7bbbba5893ee
Author: Tejun Heo <[email]>
Date: Thu Apr 21 21:32:55 2011 +0200

block: unexport DISK_EVENT_MEDIA_CHANGE for legacy/fringe drivers

In-kernel disk event polling doesn't matter for legacy/fringe drivers
and may lead to infinite event loop if ->check_events() implementation
generates events on level condition instead of edge.

Now that block layer supports suppressing exporting unlisted events,
simply leaving disk->events cleared allows these drivers to keep the
internal revalidation behavior intact while avoiding weird
interactions with userland event handler.

Reverting this particular commit fixes the bug for me.

Regression in Linux 7.0: system freeze with processes stuck in D state under load (works fine on 6.19.12)

dmesg output from working kernel 6.19.12

I am experiencing a severe system regression when upgrading from Linux 6.19.12 to 7.0.0.

On kernel 7.0.0, the system becomes progressively unresponsive under moderate to heavy load (e.g. emerge builds, module rebuilds such as NVIDIA drivers). Eventually:

- Multiple processes enter uninterruptible sleep (D state)
- TTY becomes partially responsive (input is accepted but no prompt is returned)
- System becomes effectively unusable
- Load average spikes to extremely high values (hundreds)
- Before full lockup, applications like Dolphin emulator exhibit periodic stuttering

The issue is reproducible.

Reverting back to kernel 6.19.12 completely resolves the problem. System becomes stable again with identical configuration and workload.

Hardware:
CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X
Motherboard: ASUS Crosshair VIII Hero WIFI
RAM: 64 GB
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER
Storage: ADATA LEGEND 900 PRO NVMe SSD

Software:
Distribution: Gentoo Linux
Kernel sources: gentoo-sources
Init: systemd
Desktop: KDE Plasma (Wayland)

Working kernel: 6.19.12-gentoo
Broken kernel: 7.0.0-gentoo

Steps to reproduce:
1. Boot kernel 7.0.0
2. Start a heavy workload (e.g. emerge world or NVIDIA driver module rebuild)
3. System progressively slows down
4. Eventually system becomes unresponsive and requires hard reboot

Regression: works reliably on 6.19.12, consistently fails on 7.0.0

state:
sis190 problem with changed MAC address

Hi,

I had no luck to obtain DHCP response when I changed the MAC address of eth0, which is created by sis190 module:

ifconfig eth0 down
ifconfig eth0 hw ether XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
ifconfig eth0 up

<- this was ok, MAC is ok (ISP requires it), but dhclient eth0 no luck

The problem seems to be the check of MAC address in the hardware for Rx packets, sis190.c, function sis190_init_rxfilter().

static const struct net_device_ops sis190_netdev_ops = {
...
.ndo_set_mac_address = eth_mac_addr,
...

but eth_mac_addr() does not call sis190_init_rxfilter() to change the MAC address check in the hardware. Probably it would be better to create a function like .ndo_set_mac_address = si190_set_mac_address, which would call both eth_mac_addr and sis190_init_rxfilter.

As a workaround I set eth0 to promiscuous mode, but that's not very cool :)

ifconfig eth0 promisc

state:
sis190 problem with changed MAC address

Hi,

I had no luck to obtain DHCP response when I changed the MAC address of eth0, which is created by sis190 module:

ifconfig eth0 down
ifconfig eth0 hw ether XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
ifconfig eth0 up

<- this was ok, MAC is ok (ISP requires it), but dhclient eth0 no luck

The problem seems to be the check of MAC address in the hardware for Rx packets, sis190.c, function sis190_init_rxfilter().

static const struct net_device_ops sis190_netdev_ops = {
...
.ndo_set_mac_address = eth_mac_addr,
...

but eth_mac_addr() does not call sis190_init_rxfilter() to change the MAC address check in the hardware. Probably it would be better to create a function like .ndo_set_mac_address = si190_set_mac_address, which would call both eth_mac_addr and sis190_init_rxfilter.

As a workaround I set eth0 to promiscuous mode, but that's not very cool :)

ifconfig eth0 promisc

Aquantia NIC Suspend regression

Kernel Config

When using 5.5 branch kernel my computer wouldn't go into the sleep state any longer.

Trying to sleep would almost work but the computer never really "turned off", keeping fans running. Trying to resume from that state was also absolutely impossible, as it seems the computer didn't get to sleep, hence it was not possible to wake it.

Bisecting identified 8aaa112a57c1d725c92dfad32c0694bd21b374d0 as the offending commit, which makes sense as this is "net: atlantic: refactoring pm logic". This was done directly on vanilla kernel tree.

Not sure how to exactly debug where the issue is in the code, but I can run other tests as needed.

MB: Asrock X399 Fatal1ty

state:
rt2870 driver is broken for (some) cards

The issue is described here:

[link]

in the first 2 posts.

Short summary:

"The problem appears if I run
ifconfig ra0 down
the command doesn't complete, produces no output and causes many other prolems. Examples: I lose the VT where I ran this. I can't cancel it with CTRL+C. Not even sysrq is able to recover it. Everything using PAM begins to fail, if I run sudo in a VT, i lose it (this might be related to your mounting problem). X crashes. Wicd stalls, the process can't be shut down any more. The reason fot this is that many networking applications "cylce" the interface once before using it to clear left-over configurations.
I can't even shutdown anymore if I don't use the -n option. The whole system basically goes down the drain."

Affected cards:

* Belkin F5D8053 N Wireless USB Adapter
* Trendnet USB stick

Fix:

* downgrade to 2.6.29
* or use the v2.1.2.0 drivers from [link]

First, let me know which logs and info you need and I'll attach them to the next message. I'm not a wlan expert at all. At first I'll attach kernel.log and lspci -v.

The machine is a Dell Studio XPS 1340 with a AR928X PCI Express controller.

I'm one meter far from the AP (Zyxel 600 P series) and between the notebook and the AP there are only air.
With the pre-installed Windows Vista Home the connection to the network (WAP) is almost immediately established after giving the key and the signal power is at 100%.

With the Ubuntu 8.04 kernel, 2.6.27-7 and 2.6.27-14, the signal power was about between 60 amd 80%, then after the upgrade to Ubuntu 9.04 and kernel 2.6.28-11 the wireless network doesn't worked any more. Then I compiled a shiny vanilla 2.6.30 and the situation is that I have the signal power at 80% and the access to the network is quite slow (about 20 seconds). I recompiled enabling the debug for
ath9k. In the system log I don't see anomalies or errors.

Routing determination: network.

regression.instructions: Is this bug a regression (something that used to work and broke)?

state:
Missing -I for Documentation/networking/ifenslave.c

Trying to build a 2.6.34.7 kernel with allyesconfig (I'm not crazy, I was testing a compiler) I've encountered the following problem:
gcc -Wp,-MD,Documentation/networking/.ifenslave.d -w -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -o Documentation/networking/ifenslave Documentation/networking/ifenslave.c
Documentation/networking/ifenslave.c: In function ‘get_drv_info’:
Documentation/networking/ifenslave.c:617: error: ‘BOND_ABI_VERSION’ undeclared (first use in this function)
Documentation/networking/ifenslave.c:617: error: (Each undeclared identifier is reported only once

For some reason -I for kernel include directory was missing.
Adding
HOSTCFLAGS_ifenslave.o += -I$(objtree)/usr/include
to Documentation/networking/Makefile solved the problem.

PS I've no freaking idea what this ifenslave is about, I just thought I should report that.

state:
r8152: WOL change breaks network

I use Arch Linux. Since kernel 5.18.15 (and still in 5.18.16 and 5.19), then whenever my laptop suspends my home network goes down. My Dell XPS 13 9300 model laptop is connected to a Dell WD19TB dock which is connected via ethernet network to my main home router. When the laptop suspends, it puts that dock ethernet connection in an odd state which locks up all the ethernet switch ports on that router (and thus disables the attached wifi access point which most of my family rely on). If I disconnect that ethernet cable, or the dock cable to the laptop, or wake up my laptop, then the router and network immediately recover.

It only happens when using the dock ethernet connection. If I disconnect the dock network cable but keep the dock connected and then use a USB ethernet dongle connected directly to the laptop then the problem does not occur.

Since I can reproduce the problem on call, I have bisected the kernel between previous good 5.18.14 and bad 5.18.15 and found the problem commit is [link]

I applied a revert of that commit on current Arch kernel 5.19 which is what I am currently running and of course it runs fine.

state:
Unable to distinguish encrypted and plain packets

Hi,

I have setup an IPSEC tunnel to a peer network
with isakmpd.

In order to allow the packets from the peer network
to be accepted or routed by the local router (linux),
I have to use an iptables rule which accepts packets
from that peer network. Unfortunately, there is no
way to distinguish whether the packets came through the
IPSEC tunnel or unencrypted from the internet.
So every IPSEC tunnel also is an open hole in the
iptables.

Same for outgoing packets: When packets are sent to the
peer network, but the IPSEC tunnel is not yet setup,
packets are routed unencrypted to the internet.

regards
[name]

state:
recent davej kernels (2.6.15-git*-base) eat my filesystem

Most recent kernel where this bug did not occur: 2.6.15
Distribution: Fedora Core Devel (Rawhide)
Hardware Environment: AMD64 + SATA, nforce4 chipset + sil chipset, 2 GiB mem
Software Environment: raid 1 + lvm
Problem Description:
Booting in any recent davej kernel results in lots of system errors (md, sata)
and quick filesystem corruption

Some examples :
ata5: translated ATA stat/err 0x51/04 to SCSI SK/ASC/ASCQ 0xb/00/00
ata5: status=0x51 { DriveReady SeekComplete Error }
ata5: error=0x04 { DriveStatusError }

sd 4:0:0:0: SCSI error: return code = 0x8000002
sda: Current: sense key: Medium Error
Additional sense: Unrecovered read error - auto reallocate failed
end_request: I/O error, dev sda, sector 4192831

(no idea if the problem is in the SATA layer or somewhere deeper)

More material (logs, lspci...) available in:
[link]

[PATCH] IDE Probe fails to find CD drive

System information for 2.6.30 and 2.6.31

Since updating to 2.6.31 my CD drive is no longer detected. The drive is still detected in version 2.6.30.

The offending part of dmesg appears to be:

Probing IDE interface ide1...
ide1: no devices on the port

Compared with 2.6.30's:

Probing IDE interface ide1...
hdc: PLEXTOR CD-R PX-W8432T, ATAPI CD/DVD-ROM drive
hdc: host max PIO5 wanted PIO255(auto-tune) selected PIO4
hdc: MWDMA2 mode selected

I have checked to make sure that the CD drive is set to master (it is), and have also tried kernel 2.6.32-rc5 with identical results.

I cannot find any obvious differences in the kernel configurations that may be causing the problem.

I have attached various logs / proc / config files that i think are appropriate. However, i cannot find much information that distinguishes them.

state:
#ifdef CONFIG_PM causes MPT to not compile

Most recent kernel where this bug did not occur: 2.6.17-rc3
Distribution: slack
Hardware Environment: i386
Software Environment: gcc 3.3
Problem Description: /drivers/message/fusion/mpt* using #ifdef CONFIG_PM are not
exporting the mpt_suspend mpt_resume. I do not know why we would want to
exercise power management on high-performance scsi controllers in the first
place. LSI controllers are server devices.

Steps to reproduce: compile the kernel. causes a kernel compilation failure.

Steps to fix:
comment out the #ifdef CONFIG_pm and corresponding #endif to disable this
compilation flag. recompile and the world is happy.

state:
Large USB Storage transactions hang kernel.

Distribution: Gentoo 2005.0
Hardware Environment: ix86 (PII) Desktop
Software Environment: Gentoo with either genkernel built 2.6.11-gentoo-r9 or
2.6.12-rc5; See atachments for .config and for dmesg
Problem Description:

First occurance was with 2.6.11-gentoo-r9; recurred with 2.6.12-rc5
Large transactions on a USB drive (LaCie Hard Drive Extreme Tripple 250Gb) hang
the system. Both formatting the full sized partition, and writing 100-500mb
onto a 10Gb formatted partition.

Subsequent testing showed that setting noapic and acpi=off allowed a 512mb cp to
complete. HOWEVER, I again started a 512mb cp to this drive and then when it
had about 2 minutes to go or so, I issued a `shutdown +5 min` the system then
hung once I recieve the message, system shutting down in 3 minutes. The cp did
not entirely complete, stopping at 420mb.

There are no messages on the console when this happens; system is hardlocked,
and can't be pinged.

Steps to reproduce:
CASE 1, mkfs.xfs /dev/sda1 #where dev/sda1 is a 250GB partition
CASE 2, (on a 10gb xfs partition) cp a file that's 64mb or more onto the
mounted drive.
Actual Results:
CASE 1: The drive blinked that it was busy; it kept blinking that (with out
making any discernable noise) for 8 hours. Unplugging USB had no effect. The
console was unresponsive, the network interface wouldn't respond to pings.
there were no messages from the kernel.
CASE 2: the drive blinked that it was busy for about an hour; after the first
15 second the network interface stopped responding to pings; no console
messages were printed.

CASE 3: booting with noapic and acpi=off. cp a 512mb file to the drive. Success
CASE 4: booting with noapic and acpi=off. cp a 512mb file to the drive, at
half-way shutdown the system in 5 or more minutes. It should hang before the
countdown or file cp is complete.

[it can remain hung for a whole weekend]

state:
Hang when trying to mount root fs

Distribution: Debian testing

Hardware Environment:
ASUS P4C800 Deluxe, i875 chipset ICH5 soutbridge
P4 2.80 GHz(800MHz bus)
1Gb Corsair XMS 3200 memory
hda: quantum fireball lct08
hdc: plextor cd-writer
hde: Seagate Barracuda V S-ATA, 120GB (ST3120023AS)

Software Environment:
glibc 2.3.1
gcc 3.3 (but 2.95 used to compile kernel)
reiserfs used as root fs
BLK_DEV_PIIX defined

Problem Description:
Linux hangs when it tries to mount the root fs. It looks like it's booting fine
until it comes to mounting the root fs. Then it spits out a neverending stream
of error messages of the form:
[number] handle_mm_fault
many function names are mentioned and they seem to be dealing with many things,
as I can see many words in their names like: reiser, vma, ide_intr, and others.

It also consistently says something about interrupt 5 disabled

it doesn't matter if I specify hda or hde as boot device, it works equally bad
in both cases.

Steps to reproduce:
just boot the kernel and mount a root fs.

Workaround
compile it without support for Intel PIIXn southbridge (BLK_DEV_PIIX). Then I
can bootup from my hda harddisk, but this also makes I can't access the S-ATA
harddisk.

Linux hangs when it tries to mount the root fs. It looks like it's booting fine
until it comes to mounting the root fs. Then it spits out a neverending stream
of error messages of the form:
[number] handle_mm_fault
many function names are mentioned and they seem to be dealing with many things,

it doesn't matter if I specify hda or hde as boot device, it works equally bad
in both cases.

just boot the kernel and mount a root fs.

Workaround
compile it without support for Intel PIIXn southbridge (BLK_DEV_PIIX). Then I
can bootup from my hda harddisk, but this also makes I can't access the S-ATA
harddisk.

Bluetooth - 6lowpan -- RFC7668 vs. draft - IPv6 addressing

Dear all,

my first bug report (hopefully :-)) for the Kernel ^^

Citing 6lowpan.c:675:

/* Universal/local bit set, BT 6lowpan draft ch. 3.2.1 */

If the address is identified as a public address, the original address byte get's a set bit at 2^1.
Otherwise, it will be deleted.
so far, so good. That works well, BUT:

the current RFC7668 does NOT state anything like that. Neither in ch. 3.2.1 or any other chapters I looked through.

Please tell me, am I wrong or is this a non-conform implementation?

Anyway, thank you very much for this rock-stable piece of software :-)

Best wishes, [name]

[ 67.126609] b_state=0x00000020, b_size=1024

1. bunzip2 the attached filesystem image
2. mount hdb.153 /mnt -t ext4 -o loop,errors=continue
3. rm -rf /mnt >&/dev/null

[ 67.127244] b_state=0x00000020, b_size=1024

[ 67.127573] __find_get_block_slow() failed. block=4294967296, b_blocknr=0
[ 67.127844] b_state=0x00000020, b_size=1024
... ad infinitum

state:
md/raid/udev fails to create md partition devices (/dev/mdXpY)

config 2.6.35-rc3

I'm running multiple md/raid devices, mostly raid-1, some partitioned, some not, on the same set of four spindles, identically partitioned such that partitions sd[abcd]N assemble into an md/raid device.

With kernel 2.6.34, the system boots fine, the md partition devices (mdXpY) show up in /dev, and everything mounts normally.

With kernel 2.6.35-rc3, localmount says it can't find various labeled filesystems to mount.

A bit of investigation later, I realize the only /dev/mdXpY devices showing up are the ones for the rootfs, assembled from the kernel command line. The unpartitioned md devices and the other partitioned md main devices (/dev/mdX) show up, and gdisk (the partitions are GPT, not legacy MBR) sees the partition table, which appears to be intact on the devices, but the /dev/mdXpY devices themselves (other than for the rootfs assembled from the kernel command line) don't show up.

System is a dual Opteron 290, Tyan s2885 mobo, 6 gigs RAM, running Gentoo/~amd64. All of userspace was recently fresh-rebuilt on gcc-4.5.0, which was used to compile 2.6.35-rc3 as well, tho the 2.6.34 kernel was compiled earlier with gcc 4.4.3. Related userspace apps: mdadm 3.1.2, util-linux 2.17.2, udev 154. Filesystems are reiserfs (until btrfs can safely replace it). md/raid metadata version 0.90.

As far as I can see, the only thing creating the mdXpY devices is the kernel/udev, no funny gentoo or local udev rules or initscript voodoo in that regard.

The kernel config should be attached and I can git bisect. But first:

1) This isn't already known and bisected, is it? New report?

2) No known data corruption bombs waiting to blow up the unwary git bisector in the 2.6.35 development series, I hope? (That's why I wait until rc2 or so before testing, any data corruption bombs should be fixed by then, hopefully.)

device 168c:0012 rev 1)
Software Environment: gkrellm 2.1.16-2 Debian package in unstable
Problem Description: The statistics on data traffic in and out are incorrect.
When using gkrellm (and apparently other similar network statistics gathering
software) the network interface reports zero transfer for one second, then the
summation of two seconds of transfers for the next second, then zero bytes for
the following second and so on and so on.

The following URL shows a recent discussion on USENET of the identical problem:

[link]

The link actually produces a fix that works, although technically is ment to be
incorrect. For me the alteration of
linux-2.6.0-test4/drivers/net/e1000/e1000_main.c and making line 1394:

mod_timer(&adapter->watchdog_timer, HZ);

fixes the problem. I understand though that this apparently sets up a timer
event thats in the past. Hey it works for me though.....

Steps to reproduce: run gkrellm on a ethernet card being monitored by gkrellm
that uses the e1000 driver. Download a file and look at the strange results.

state:
Linux 6.4.4 Regression: MariaDB (mysqld) causes one core of the CPU to use 100% with io-wait operations.

OS: Arch Linux

Linux 6.4.4 introduces 100% usage in one core of the CPU with io-wait operations when MariaDB 11.0.2 (mysqld process) is running, even if the database is completely empty, this problem still occurs.

To prevent this bug for happening it is necessary to downgrade to Linux <6.4.3. Linux 6.4.4 without Arch Linux patches, Linux Mainline 6.5-rc1 and 6.5-rc2 don't fix the problem either.

Strangely there is also no sign that the mysqld process is using an absurd amount of io-wait on the processor core, it was found by purely discarding and killing processes until the processor core usage was normal and without io-wait operations. No tool to monitor I/O operations to find was able to find that mysqld was the cause of this bug (not even top).

I also used different commits prior to the 6.4.4 release using `git bisect` and none of them introduced this bug. There is no journal logs nor dmesg logs related to this bug. It independent of the file system used (I guess, it happens on EXT4 and BTRFS, but it doesn't seem to be related with the file system either)

How to reproduce it?:
- Install and use the Linux 6.4.4 Release
- Install MariaDB, initialize a empty database and run the process with your preferred init system
- Use htop or top to see the high io-wait usage in one core of the CPU

Arch Linux forums thread (Where we tested different kernel commits and there is other people with the same problem): [link]

If i need to provide more information, just ask for it...

(This bug was found originally because i use Akonadi, a PIM layer made by KDE Plasma developers that uses MariaDB/MySQL to store data)

To prevent this bug for happening it is necessary to downgrade to Linux <6.4.3. Linux 6.4.4 without Arch Linux patches, Linux Mainline 6.5-rc1 and 6.5-rc2 don't fix the problem either.

Strangely there is also no sign that the mysqld process is using an absurd amount of io-wait on the processor core, it was found by purely discarding and killing processes until the processor core usage was normal and without io-wait operations. No tool to monitor I/O operations to find was able to find that mysqld was the cause of this bug (not even top).

I also used different commits prior to the 6.4.4 release using `git bisect` and none of them introduced this bug. There is no journal logs nor dmesg logs related to this bug. It independent of the file system used (I guess, it happens on EXT4 and BTRFS, but it doesn't seem to be related with the file system either)

How to reproduce it?:
- Install and use the Linux 6.4.4 Release
- Install MariaDB, initialize a empty database and run the process with your preferred init system
- Use htop or top to see the high io-wait usage in one core of the CPU

If i need to provide more information, just ask for it...

(This bug was found originally because i use Akonadi, a PIM layer made by KDE Plasma developers that uses MariaDB/MySQL to store data)

sch_teql no longer works post 2.6.30

Patch to fix sch_teql

The sch_teql module, which can be used to load balance over a set of underlying interfaces, stopped working after 2.6.30 and has been broken in all kernels since then.

The problem is that the transmit routine relies on being able to access the destination address in the skb in order to do ARP resolution once it has decided which underlying interface it is going to transmit through.

In 2.6.31 the IFF_XMIT_DST_RELEASE flag was introduced, and set by default for all interfaces, which causes the destination address to be release before the transmit routine for the interface is called.

The solution (implemented in the attached patch) is to clear that flag for teql interfaces.

Journal from the day it crashed

I have a Dell Inspiron 2405 2-in-1 with an Intel AX200 rev 1a, and I'm using iwd. My router is an ASUS RT-AX58U.

Occasionally, about one or two times per day, the card firmware will crash and does not recover on its own (I can recover it by removing and reloading iwlmvm).
Presumably this is when my AP decides to initiate a channel switch.

I've noticed that this seems to usually happen when I'm not at my computer, but it sometimes does happen while I'm using it.

I'm not sure when this started happening, because this didn't happen often enough for me to notice with the APs at my university (maybe they were on 5ghz so they didn't need to switch channels often?).

I've attached my journal from the time my system booted to the time of the error.

Some of the memory blocks kcalloc'ed in
ath5k_eeprom_convert_pcal_info_*() are not freed even when module ath5k is
unloaded.

To reproduce the problem, it is enough to load ath5k.ko module and then unload it again.

Here is the trace for one iteration of the outer 'for' loop with my comments.
ath5k_eeprom_convert_pcal_info_2413(),
drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath5k/eeprom.c:1148:

// Allocation of chinfo[pier].pd_curves, line 1153. Room for 4 elements of
// type struct ath5k_pdgain_info is created.
called___kmalloc: (.text+0x212f) arguments: (48, 80d0), result: ab3ad780

// The inner loop, iter #0, allocation of pd->pd_step and pd->pd_pwr
// for chinfo[pier].pd_curves[pdgain_idx[0]] (lines 1176 and 1182)
called___kmalloc: (.text+0x212f) arguments: (4, 80d0), result: ab1c3f68
called___kmalloc: (.text+0x212f) arguments: (8, 80d0), result: ab1c3f70

// The inner loop, iter #1, allocation of pd->pd_step and pd->pd_pwr

called___kmalloc: (.text+0x212f) arguments: (5, 80d0), result: ab1c3f78
called___kmalloc: (.text+0x212f) arguments: (10, 80d0), result: ab17ce80
<...>

Here is the trace for one iteration of the outer 'for' loop,
ath5k_eeprom_free_pcal_info(),
drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath5k/eeprom.c:1564

// The inner loop, iter #0, line 1573
called_kfree: (.text+0x20be) arguments: ((null))
called_kfree: (.text+0x20c6) arguments: ((null))

// The inner loop, iter #1, line 1573
called_kfree: (.text+0x20be) arguments: (ab1c3f78)
called_kfree: (.text+0x20c6) arguments: (ab17ce80)

ath5k_eeprom_convert_pcal_info_*() and ath5k_eeprom_free_pcal_info().
